source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in Language Models
finding: GAP 5 resolved. Re-read of appendix Table 11 (thinking models, Wason rule discovery) gives the Qwen3-32B figures. Baseline task success 0.413; Dual-Goal 0.600; Think-in-Opposites (TiO) 0.613. The earlier 0.33 to 0.63 reading mixed the non-thinking baseline (0.325) with the thinking TiO value.
numbers: Thinking Qwen3-32B: 0.413 to 0.613 (TiO), turns until success 10.83 to 6.38, I:C 0.14 to 0.54 (Table 3). Non-thinking Qwen3-32B: 0.325 baseline, Dual-Goal 0.100, TiO 0.362. Thinking Qwen3-8B: 0.212 to 0.363 (TiO), 0.400 (Dual-Goal).
limits: Table 11 text layout is garbled in PDF extraction; rows were matched using the turn counts that agree with Table 3.
agent_relevance: Correct b18/b19 to 0.41 to 0.61 for Qwen3-32B thinking. The prompt-only gain is real for thinking models.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in Language Models
finding: Significance and boundary: the prompt interventions help thinking models but not reliably non-thinking ones. Paired permutation tests over episode pairs, 50,000 permutations.
numbers: Thinking models: Dual-Goal +0.148 task success (p<2e-5), TiO +0.123 (p<2e-5); I:C +0.375 and +0.168. Non-thinking: Dual-Goal -0.060 (p=.0065, harmful), TiO +0.063 (p=.0033); I:C change not significant (p=.24, p=.60).
limits: Same authors, one task family (number-triple rules). No independent replication found.
agent_relevance: A think-of-counterexamples instruction is safe for reasoning-mode models; a forced two-goal prompt can hurt non-reasoning ones. Gate by model type.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in Language Models
finding: GAP 3 partial: equal-token test is not satisfied. Thinking-model prompts that raise the incompatible-test ratio also raise tokens per turn. Row identified by matching turn counts.
numbers: Qwen3-8B thinking: mean tokens per turn 1088 (baseline) vs about 2142 (the row with 7.37 turns to success, which matches TiO in Table 3). Qwen3-32B: 1030 baseline vs 1472. Turns until success fall (10.83 to 6.38 for 32B), so total tokens per solved episode may be near equal; the paper does not report it.
limits: Row labels lost in PDF extraction, so the token attribution is inferred, not stated. Totals per episode not reported.
agent_relevance: Any test of falsification prompts in our agent must log total tokens per solved item, not tokens per turn.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in Language Models
finding: GAP 3 partial: second task (Blicket detector, 192 episodes) tests transfer of Think-in-Opposites. Gains are mixed in direction.
limits: Same authors, same intervention, a relative of the original task (hidden-rule discovery). Not a natural-task replication such as diagnosis or QA. Dual-Goal not tested because no opposite hypothesis exists.
agent_relevance: Gain concentrates in thinking models and shrinks when the baseline is already high (ceiling). Treat falsification prompts as helpful on rule-search style problems only.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) AgentCDM: Enhancing Multi-Agent Collaborative Decision-Making via ACH-Inspired Structured Reasoning
finding: GAP 4 partial: first LLM test with baselines that uses an ACH protocol (Step 3 'Construct Hypothesis-Evidence Matrix') as the decision agent's prompt. A zero-shot ACH prompt beats an unstructured Informed Dictatorial decider and six voting rules, by a small margin.
numbers: Table 1 (accuracy %, 4 base models on MMLU, MMLU-Pro, ARC-C; change vs single agent, All Average row): voting rules about +0.0 to +0.1 (some -0.6 to -0.2 in the dictatorial rows); ACH Homogeneous +2.0 (67.9); Qwen-7B-R1 as ACH decider +1.6; trained AgentCDM +8.6 to +11.6. Text says the ACH prompt beats the informed decider by 1.9 points on All Average.
limits: Multiple-choice knowledge questions, not analyst sensemaking. Table text is garbled (row misalignment), so the All Average figures are partly inferred. ACH is not isolated from any structured prompt. Token cost not equalised. Large gains come from training.
agent_relevance: A hypothesis-by-evidence matrix prompt gives a small positive gain at the decision step; the large gains need training of the decider, which we cannot do.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) AgentCDM: Enhancing Multi-Agent Collaborative Decision-Making via ACH-Inspired Structured Reasoning
finding: Rigid ACH scaffolding alone hurts: after stage-1 training on ACH-style traces only, accuracy fell below a plain prompt. Both stages needed.
numbers: Table 4 (MMLU / MMLU-Pro / ARC-C): Full 78.5 / 65.2 / 96.0; Vanilla prompt 72.6 / 52.5 / 89.0; Scaffolding-Only 68.1 / 49.4 / 84.0; Exploration-Only 71.5 / 52.1 / 89.7.
limits: Training-based ablation, so it speaks to learned scaffolds, not prompts. One run, no CIs.
agent_relevance: Supports schema section 4b caution: a fixed ritual of steps can lower accuracy unless the model may deviate from it.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) LLM-as-an-Investigator: Evidence-First Agentic Reasoning for Robust Interactive Problem Diagnosis
finding: GAP 2 and GAP 4 partial: a Solution Investigator Agent (SIA) with an explicit hypothesis and evidence record, a counterfactual critic and a separate verifier beats thinking, interactive, ReAct and ToT baselines on forum-derived diagnosis cases (303 built, 100 evaluated).
numbers: Final score /100 [95% CI]: SIA 79.2 [72.7, 83.7]; THK-int (thinking plus interaction, no explicit state) 72.8 [66.8, 79.8]; Ask-5 72.3; ReAct 69.0; THK 67.5; BAS 67.3; ToT 61.5. Questions asked: SIA 5.2 vs 3.7 (THK-int). Other backbones: GPT-5.6 Terra 75.4 vs 69.2; Claude Sonnet 5 76.1 vs 68.4.
limits: CIs overlap between SIA and THK-int. Authors call differences descriptive. SIA asks more questions and records more hypotheses, so interaction cost is not equalised. Simulated user, LLM-judged. Model names taken from the source.
agent_relevance: Gain over the same model without an explicit written hypothesis-evidence record is about 6 to 7 points, but confounded with more questions.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) LLM-as-an-Investigator: Evidence-First Agentic Reasoning for Robust Interactive Problem Diagnosis
finding: Component ablation of SIA. Counterfactual critique and the structured investigation state matter most; evidence-weight updates matter least.
numbers: Final / potential: Full 79.2 / 89.2; without structured investigation 72.8 / 84.7; without counterfactual critique 74.0 / 85.5; without follow-up questions 75.0 / 85.0; without hypothesis expansion 76.5 / 79.3; without final adjudication 76.0 / 89.2; without weight updates 78.5 / 88.5.
limits: Single run on 100 cases, no CIs for ablations, one backbone in the table. Removing a component changes the number of calls, so tokens are not equalised.
agent_relevance: A step that argues against the leading hypothesis is worth about 5 points here; numeric weight updating is nearly worthless, so skip it in our scaffold.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) LLM-as-an-Investigator: Evidence-First Agentic Reasoning for Robust Interactive Problem Diagnosis
finding: Anchoring test: a plausible but wrong user conjecture lowers SIA only a little because the conjecture is held as a hypothesis, not as evidence.
numbers: 10 paired cases. Final score 80.0 control vs 76.0 challenged; potential 90.0 vs 85.0; exact diagnosis 6/10 vs 5/10; wrong suggested cause selected in 2/10; lower score in 3/10.
limits: N=10 and a non-random subset chosen to allow a plausible alternative. No baseline run on the same pairs, so no evidence that explicit state resists anchoring better than a plain loop.
agent_relevance: Keep user or prior claims in a separate conjecture slot, never as evidence.

source: West and Dragut (2026) PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
finding: GAP 6 answered in part: prompt-only (no RL, no fine-tuning) patch-switching policies based on information scent and realised yield beat no-switching, a focused crawler and a trained search agent on live-web collection. Scent comes from an LLM Forager scoring links in batches of up to 16.
limits: The best scent policy is only slightly better than Fixed-Reseed (switch after a fixed page count) and loses on Universities (15.5 vs 16.1). Realized-yield policies have high harvest rate but low coverage. Single run per cell, no CIs. Task is corpus collection, not question answering.
agent_relevance: Most of the gain comes from switching at all; scent adds a smaller increment. A fixed-budget then-move-on rule is a cheap baseline.

source: West and Dragut (2026) PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
finding: Token-matched comparison (appendix Table 8) against the trained DeepResearcher-7B and commercial deep-research tools. PatchScout variants truncated to DeepResearcher's token budget still visit far more pages.
numbers: Pages visited at the same token budget: DeepResearcher 78, 56, 28, 64; Scent-EMA 951, 1223, 1664, 1491. Coverage % (4 topics): DeepResearcher 0.3, 0.8, 1.0, 17.3; Scent-EMA 5.6, 7.6, 40.1, 12.8; Fixed-Reseed 5.7, 6.0, 34.0, 8.3; Gemini Deep Research 1.8, 3.0, 93.4 (law), final unmatched; Claude Deep Research 1.1, 15.0, 91.9 (law).
limits: On the Autism topic DeepResearcher (17.3) beats Scent-EMA (12.8) at matched tokens. On Law schools the commercial tools reach 92 to 93% coverage from one report, far above PatchScout's token-matched 40%. Commercial tools cannot be truncated. The per-page Critic costs about 158 tokens per page.
agent_relevance: The equal-token test exists here and still favours switching policies on broad topics, but not on sparse short-list topics.

source: West and Dragut (2026) PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
finding: Ablations (Table 9): the timing of the switch and the scent signal both matter, and adaptive queries beat all-upfront queries.
numbers: Coverage % (4 topics): Scent-EMA full 15.5, 24.6, 86.8, 35.3. Random-Reseed 4.6, 2.2, 25.4, 9.0. Upfront-Scout 1.2, 2.0, 11.7, 12.0. Random-Forager 8.3, 6.6, 28.9, 10.5.
limits: Row mapping in the garbled table was matched by the Scent-EMA and Realized-EMA reference rows. Single run per cell.
agent_relevance: Feedback from earlier results should shape later queries: a write-then-read history beats planning all queries up front.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States (Table 2 and Table 3 re-read)
finding: GAP 2 and GAP 1 proxy: the nearest equal-cost test of a written evidence state vs history-as-context. Removing the epistemic state (same foraging actions, ReAct style) costs 7.7 points at almost the same token cost (28.3k vs 29.7k). The manipulated factor is the split between acting trace and evidence state; forage and sense loops are not separated.
numbers: LOOGLE-V2: full 78.2 at 29.7k tokens; w/o epistemic state 70.5 (-7.7) at 28.3k; w/o foraging actions 17.7; w/o file tools 74.2; w/o grounding 75.5. Table 3 (Qwen2.5-72B, LOOGLE-V2): vanilla LLM 24.0, SCOUT interface 28.3; after SFT LLM 25.1 vs SCOUT 55.4.
limits: Tasks run up to 1M tokens and do not fit in context; the question whether a written state helps on tasks that do fit is untested. Single runs. RL training drives most Table 3 gains.
agent_relevance: The 7.7-point gain at equal cost supports a compact, source-anchored evidence note kept apart from the action log. It does not test forage-vs-sense splitting.

source: Jiang (2025) Workflow is All You Need: DeepNews (Experiment 4.1 design re-read)
finding: GAP 9: the context-size effect is not decomposed. The experiment varies one factor, retrieved context length, and nothing separates redundancy from volume or relevance.
numbers: 20 financial topics x 5 context sizes (5k, 10k, 15k, 30k, 40k characters) = 100 reports. Hallucination-free rate: under 20% below 10k; 40% at 15k; 85% at 30k; 90% at 40k. With 20 reports per cell, one report is 5 points; no CI, no repeats, no variance reported.
limits: The minimum necessary redundancy reading comes from naming a ratio (about 10:1 input to output), not from a control that holds volume fixed and varies redundancy. One domain (Chinese financial news).
agent_relevance: Do not copy a 30k-character rule. A redundancy-vs-volume ablation is still needed.

source: Pirolli and Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology (Figure 6 text re-read)
finding: GAP 7 closed negatively: Figure 6 is a notional cost-structure graph, not data. The text only asserts that expert analysts set filters lower, accept more noise, and reject unimportant messages faster than less expert analysts.
numbers: No sample, no values, no units. Text: the expert analyst gets more relevant information in a shorter time (the higher curve).
quote: the expert analyst can get more of the relevant information in a shorter amount of time (the higher curve)
limits: Claim rests on cognitive task analysis with a few analysts (not reported here). No later measured test of the curve was found in the sources opened.
agent_relevance: Do not build an analyst-skill learning curve into the scaffold from this paper.
